callees_treated_as_inputs: the spot scale selector at 0x5a01310, a direct call at 0x5a010a3: its body is the open RE-001-spot-scale-select-1310-115 packet's question (PR #3320); only its return value (scale, at least 1 under that packet's pinned behaviour) is used here, and the final division relies on that: a scale of 0 would fault the binary and is excluded by the model as unreachable through this callee

census.caller_value: all four call sites load the f64 constant 0.1 at 0x4593e0 into xmm0; sites 0x54f0797 and 0x54f1d67 also pass the constant flag 1, the other two pass a stack byte

constants.0x4559c0: (-0.0, -0.0) pair: negation mask for the wrapper, sign source for the leaf
constants.0x458d58: 2^64-2048, the largest f64 below 2^64 (cast saturation threshold)
constants.0x4593e0: 0.1 (the value all four call sites pass)

front.conversion: rcx is converted to an f64 by the magic sequence at 0x5a00fdc..0x5a00ff9: movq, punpckldq against the dwords at 0x451210 (0x43300000, 0x45300000), subpd against the pair at 0x450170 (2^52, 2^84), unpckhpd, addsd; the result is the correctly rounded (f64)n
front.negation: if edx != 0, xmm0 is xorpd-ed against the (-0.0, -0.0) pair at 0x4559c0 (site 0x5a00fd4): v is negated
front.product: xmm0 = (v + 1.0) * (f64)n; the 1.0 constant is at 0x4592b0 (addsd site 0x5a00ffd, mulsd site 0x5a01005)

limits: The leaf's own caller census is not taken here: the claim is only that this wrapper reaches it through slot 0x64e1890, not that the wrapper is its only caller.
v and n are pinned as the wrapper's raw register inputs; which semantic quantities the four callers place in rcx is their own routines' question and is not claimed here.

The selector's return is an input. The model raises ValueError on scale == 0 as a model safety property; the binary would fault, and the pinned selector contract (scale >= 1) makes the case unreachable through this wrapper.
Native execution, a Rust rebuild and byte equivalence are not claimed.

reference.cast: the saturating f64-to-u64 sequence at 0x5a01017..0x5a01096: the absolute bit pattern is compared against 0x7fefffffffffffff; only +inf takes the greater branch, which skips the clamp with the scratch register still 0.0, so +inf casts as 0.0; finite values are clamped above by 2^64 (constant at 0x459090) and put through the two-part cvttsd2si pair (subtracting 2^63, constant at 0x459360); a value above 2^64-2048 (constant at 0x458d58) keeps u64::MAX instead
reference.clamp_below: maxsd against +0.0 at 0x5a01013: a negative or NaN rounded value becomes +0.0
reference.raise_to_one: cmp r12, 1 / adc r12, 0 at 0x5a01092: a cast result of exactly 0 becomes 1

relationships: PR #3320 (open, RE-001-spot-scale-select-1310-115) pins the selector at 0x5a01310 this wrapper calls; that packet cites this wrapper as a caller context but does not enter it
PR #3315 (open, RE-001-pow10-scale-01110-115) pins the perp selector at 0x5a01110, which the wrapper never calls; the questions are disjoint
the round leaf at 0x63efe40 is cited as a stored string in the merged RE-001-node115-bole-entry-counter-order packet's records; a citation is not a pin of its semantics, which this packet supplies

round_leaf.caller_census_note: the census in this packet covers the wrapper only; the leaf's other callers are not counted here
round_leaf.reached_via: call qword ptr [0x64e1890] at 0x5a01009; the slot's R_X86_64_RELATIVE addend is 0x63efe40
round_leaf.semantics: round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero: s = x + copysign(0.49999999999999994, x) (constant pair at 0x450e60, sign mask pair at 0x4559c0); when the biased exponent of s exceeds 0x432, s is returned; otherwise the fraction bits below the binary point are cleared (a sign-only mask when |s| < 1), so a negative input in (-1, 0) yields -0.0 and an input of exactly +/-0.5 yields +/-1.0

rounding.choice: the flag selects q (flag == 0) or q + 1 (flag != 0); the increment at 0x5a010cb saturates: when q == u64::MAX the wrapped 0 is replaced by u64::MAX (cmove at 0x5a010d5)
rounding.division: when (reference | scale) >> 32 == 0 a 32-bit div is used (site 0x5a010c6), else a 64-bit div (site 0x5a010bc); both leave the same quotient q = reference / scale
rounding.multiply_back: the chosen count is multiplied by scale (mul at 0x5a010e2); on overflow the result stays u64::MAX; a product of exactly 0 is raised to 1 (cmp/adc at 0x5a010ea)

routine.question: Given the pinned selector as a callee, what integer does the wrapper return for (flag, v, n, scale), and how is that integer computed stage by stage?
routine.signature: (rdi = object, rsi = second argument, edx = flag, xmm0 = f64 value v, rcx = u64 n) -> rax u64; rdi and rsi are forwarded unchanged to the selector call and play no other role

selector_call.arguments: (rdi = the wrapper's object, rsi = the wrapper's second argument, rdx = the reference)
selector_call.relationship: the selector's own input/output behaviour is the question of the open RE-001-spot-scale-select-1310-115 packet (PR #3320); here its return value is an input called scale
